snippet.title: The BBC Actually Told Diana The King Planned to MURDER Her
snippet.description:
In this explosive episode of Heretics, investigative journalist Andy Webb joins us to uncover the extraordinary story behind Princess Diana, Martin Bashir, and the BBC’s most controversial interview in history.

Get Andy Webb's book Dianarama here: https://www.amazon.co.uk/Dianarama-Betrayal-Princess-Andy-Webb-ebook/dp/B0F624Q672

Webb — whose work has forced the BBC into unprecedented scrutiny — breaks down how Bashir allegedly used forged documents, fake bank statements, and fear-driven manipulation to win Diana’s trust and secure the infamous 1995 Panorama interview.

Were the consequences more devastating than anyone imagined? Webb explores the shocking possibility that without that interview, Diana might be alive today, living quietly as a grandmother at 64.

We dig into the biggest unanswered questions:

- Who was Martin Bashir—and how did he get so close to Diana and Michael Jackson?
- How did forged bank statements open the gates of Kensington Palace?
- What was Diana told that terrified her into believing people at the highest levels wanted her dead?
- Why did she record what was essentially her “last will and testament”?
- How did a bodyguard she cared about die only months after their relationship?
- What did the BBC know—and when did they know it?
- Why did the corporation spend over £1 million of licence fee money to stop Webb’s investigations?

Andy Webb reveals how Diana felt duped, hoaxed, and frightened, how rumours involving Tiggy Legge-Bourke spiralled out of control, and how the BBC’s internal decisions continue to raise questions about accountability, leadership, and the culture that allowed Bashir’s behavior to go unchecked.

If you want to understand the real story behind the Bashir scandal, the BBC cover-up, and the chain of events that reshaped the Royal Family forever, this is the episode you can't miss.

snippet.title: Princess Diana interview: BBC covered up ‘deceitful behaviour’ of journalist Martin Bashir
snippet.description:
Princess Diana's brother Earl Spencer says he draws a line between the Panorama interview and his sister's death in Paris. Her jaw-dropping revelations had been watched the world over. 

Panorama reporter Martin Bashir won numerous awards for his 1995 scoop,  which the BBC has started to return. But he had secured the interview after faking bank statements to suggest royal insiders were betraying Diana to the tabloids. According to the inquiry report when questions were raised, the BBC top brass believed Mr Bashir's lies in an internal investigation damned today as "woefully inadequate".

snippet.title: How Martin Bashir Destroyed Michael Jackson's Life – Andy Webb
snippet.description:
Investigative journalist Andy Webb joins Andrew Gold to expose how Martin Bashir’s reporting helped destroy Michael Jackson’s life — and why the truth about Bashir’s tactics has only recently begun to surface. Webb has spent years uncovering the darker side of Bashir’s journalism, and in this explosive conversation he reveals how the same deceptive methods used in the Princess Diana scandal were also deployed against the world’s biggest pop star. If you enjoy fearless breakdowns like this, make sure you subscribe to Heretics Clips: https://www.youtube.com/@hereticsclips/videos

In this gripping clip, Andy Webb walks through how Bashir earned Michael Jackson’s trust, how he gained unprecedented access, and how that access was later weaponised in a way that Jackson never saw coming. Webb explains how the resulting documentary reshaped the public’s perception of Jackson overnight, opening the door to years of scrutiny, accusations, and global media hostility that the singer struggled to escape.

But how much of what viewers saw was manipulated? And did Michael Jackson truly understand the type of journalist he was dealing with? Andy Webb breaks down the behind-the-scenes negotiations, the promises that were allegedly made, and the moments that never made it to air — moments that, according to Webb, reveal an entirely different picture of Jackson’s intentions and Bashir’s agenda.

He also explains how Bashir’s portrayal of Jackson triggered an avalanche of consequences: raids, investigations, courtroom battles, relentless media pressure, and a dramatic collapse in Jackson’s health, career, and mental well-being. Webb argues that Bashir’s framing didn’t just damage Jackson’s reputation — it changed the trajectory of his life.

What were Bashir’s motives? Why were his tactics not exposed sooner? And how did one documentary help shape a narrative that Jackson would spend the rest of his life fighting? Webb answers these questions with forensic detail, showing the parallels between Bashir’s earlier actions and the patterns that re-emerged during his work with Jackson.

If you’ve ever wondered what really happened behind the documentary that turned the world against Michael Jackson — and the role Martin Bashir played in that downfall — this conversation provides the clearest explanation yet.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2qq9fcGZTKM

snippet.title: Michael Jackson Trusted Him — Then the Interview Aired
snippet.description:
Michael Jackson trusted journalist Martin Bashir with unprecedented access to Neverland—but when *Living with Michael Jackson* aired, Michael called it a betrayal. This documentary examines how Bashir gained Michael Jackson’s trust, how the interview was edited, and how it changed the public’s view of him forever.

For eight months, Martin Bashir followed Michael Jackson through Neverland, hotel rooms and private moments with his children. Michael believed he was finally being given a chance to tell his story honestly. Instead, the broadcast became one of the most damaging moments of his life.

But Michael’s decision to trust Bashir was not as naive as it may appear.

Bashir was already famous for his interview with Princess Diana—the one interview that made Michael believe he could safely open up. Years later, an official inquiry revealed that Bashir had used forged documents and deception to secure Diana’s trust.

So was Michael Jackson targeted using the same playbook?

In this episode of The Recall, we revisit the making of *Living with Michael Jackson*, the footage Michael’s team recorded behind the scenes, the public backlash, the 2005 trial and the later revelations surrounding Martin Bashir’s interview methods.

Was Michael Jackson simply too trusting—or was the entire interview engineered from the beginning?

Share your opinion in the comments.

Subscribe to **The Recall** for celebrity documentaries, forgotten interviews, cultural history and the truth behind the stories people thought they already knew.

For eight months, Martin Bashir followed Michael Jackson through Neverland, hotel rooms and private moments with his children. Michael believed he was finally being given a chance to tell his story honestly. Instead, the broadcast became one of the most damaging moments of his life.

But Michael’s decision to trust Bashir was not as naive as it may appear.

Bashir was already famous for his interview with Princess Diana—the one interview that made Michael believe he could safely open up. Years later, an official inquiry revealed that Bashir had used forged documents and deception to secure Diana’s trust.

So was Michael Jackson targeted using the same playbook?

In this episode of The Recall, we revisit the making of *Living with Michael Jackson*, the footage Michael’s team recorded behind the scenes, the public backlash, the 2005 trial and the later revelations surrounding Martin Bashir’s interview methods.

Was Michael Jackson simply too trusting—or was the entire interview engineered from the beginning?

snippet.title: Martin Bashir 'has Michael Jackson's blood on his hands' after documentary
snippet.description: Martin Bashir has been accused of having 'blood on his hands' in regards to his explosive fly-on-the-wall documentary with pop singer Michael Jackson.   The journalist and news anchor conducted a series of interviews with the King of Pop in 2003, but now he has been accused of setting him up.   Jackson's former confidant and lawyer Brian Oxman claims Bashir wanted him "brought down" on TV like Princess Diana – sparking a chain of events that led to the star’s 2009 overdose death.   The claims come after police said they may probe Bashir’s 1995 Panorama interview with Princess Diana, if a complaint is made.    Diana's brother Earl Spencer has alleged Bashir showed him fake financial papers and lied about the royals to get access to his sibling back in 1995.  During his interview with Jackson, Bashir allegedly "induced" the father-of-three into making admissions after praising his "parenting skills".  Living with Michael Jackson saw Jackson admit to Bashir that he let kids sleep in his bed at his Neverland Ranch.    It also showed Jackson holding hands and discussing sleeping arrangements with a 12-year-old boy.  In December 2003, Santa Barbara authorities charged Jackson with seven counts of child molestation and two counts of intoxicating a minor with alcoholic drinks.  Jackson denied the allegations and pleaded not guilty, and his trial began in January 2005.   Oxman believes the molestation trial "tormented Jackson until the day he passed".  He told The Mirror: "Some of the family feel Martin Bashir has blood on his hands.  "He brought down Princess Diana on TV. He wanted to do the same with the biggest entertainer in the world.  "Michael was cleared on all counts, but these false accusations meant whatever he did, a cloud hung over him."   On the ITV documentary, watched by over 500 million worldwide, Bashir called Neverland a "dangerous place for a vulnerable child".  However, Oxman claims that Jackson’s footage has Bashir saying "it was a privilege" to film him helping sick kids and that misrepresentation of that would be "disgusting".  In unaired scenes he apparently said: "It almost makes me weep. Your interaction is just so natural, loving."   Jackson was cleared of the allegations in 2005 and unearthed legal papers show his lawyers had tried to make Bashir take the stand.  They accused Bashir of continuous misrepresentation and lying "over and over again", promising him that it would be a "positive film".  But Bashir avoided cross-examination about his methods to gain interviews by using an obscure local law that essentially protects journalists from divulging details of unaired interactions.  Oxman added: "Michael was fuming. Bashir had many questions to answer."   Jackson’s lawyers wanted Bashir to be questioned and "held in contempt" but the judge never ruled on the matter.  Jackson passed away on June 25, 2009, from cardiac arrest less than three weeks before his This Is It show was due to begin in London.  Daily Star has contacte

Martin Bashir 'used Princess Diana letter to land Michael Jackson interview' - new claims
FORMER BBC journalist Martin Bashir has been hit by fresh accusations in the wake of Lord Dyson's report into his 1995 Panorama interview with Princess Diana. 
Friends and family of Michael Jackson fear the reporter used rogue methods to secure a sitdown with the star.
Disgraced journalist Martin Bashir has been accused of using a letter of commendation from Princess Diana to secure an interview with mega pop star Michael Jackson. 
The singer's brother Tito and nephew Taj Jackson and close friend of Michael and Diana's, 
Uri Geller have aired their fears Mr Bashir hoodwinked Mr Jackson in the same way he did Diana.
Lord Dyson's report found Mr Bashir showed forged bank statements to Diana's brother Earl Spencer who later introduced the reporter to the princess.

The damning report highlighted the BBC's systematic failure to deal with Mr Bashir correctly 
and saw the organisation slammed by both Prince William, and Prince Harry, 36.

Now Michael Jackson's family and friends have accused Mr Bashir of using "unethical tactics" to land his infamous Neverland documentary with the star.
The singer's nephew Taj wrote online: “Bashir’s manipulated footage and unethical journalism is one of the main reasons my uncle is not here today."
He added: "That trial broke him. Shame on those who provided cover for Bashir. Shame on those who rewarded him. 
My family deserve an investigation and apology too.”

Michael's brother Tito claimed: “Bashir created a fake narrative about my brother, 
which becomes crystal clear when you view the out-takes Bashir kept secret.

"He used Michael’s trust and friendship with Diana to get the interview,
manipulated Michael throughout the interview, then deceptively edited the footage.”
Mutual friend of Diana and Michael, celebrity psychic Uri Geller claims Bashir produced a letter purportedly from Diana to gain access to Jackson, 
who was best man when he renewed his vows in 2001.

Mr Geller said it was this letter that convinced him to introduce Mr Bashir to Jackson.

He told the Mirror: “What convinced me to introduce him to Michael was a letter he pulled out of his pocket.

“It was folded two or three times and there was a logo on it.

snippet.title: MICHAEL JACKSON'S FURY: How the Media Betrayed the King of Pop
snippet.description:
Michael Jackson trusted journalist Martin Bashir with unprecedented access to his private life. When the documentary aired in 2003, the King of Pop was furious — and accused the interviewer of betrayal.

But Michael Jackson had something the public hadn't seen: footage from another camera.

In this documentary, we investigate one of the most explosive media controversies in Michael Jackson's career — and the interviews that led to it.

From Oprah Winfrey's revealing 1993 interview to Diane Sawyer's uncomfortable questions in 1995 and Barbara Walters' confrontation in 1997, Michael Jackson repeatedly found himself defending his personal life in front of millions.

Then came Martin Bashir.

For months, Bashir filmed Michael Jackson at Neverland Ranch and beyond. His documentary, Living with Michael Jackson, sparked international controversy and raised serious questions about the singer's conduct.

Jackson accused Bashir of misrepresenting him. Bashir denied those accusations.

When Michael's team released additional behind-the-scenes footage, viewers saw a striking contrast between Bashir's private praise and his critical documentary.

The controversy eventually became connected to the criminal proceedings against Jackson. In June 2005, Michael Jackson was acquitted on all counts.

This film explores the interviews, the hidden-camera controversy, the public response, and the complicated relationship between one of the world's biggest entertainers and the journalists who questioned him.

Was Michael Jackson betrayed by the media — or was the truth more complicated?

Michael Jackson trusted journalist Martin Bashir with unprecedented access to his private life. When the documentary aired in 2003, the King of Pop was furious — and accused the interviewer of betrayal.

In this documentary, we investigate one of the most explosive media controversies in Michael Jackson's career — and the interviews that led to it.

From Oprah Winfrey's revealing 1993 interview to Diane Sawyer's uncomfortable questions in 1995 and Barbara Walters' confrontation in 1997, Michael Jackson repeatedly found himself defending his personal life in front of millions.

Then came Martin Bashir.

For months, Bashir filmed Michael Jackson at Neverland Ranch and beyond. His documentary, Living with Michael Jackson, sparked international controversy and raised serious questions about the singer's conduct.

Jackson accused Bashir of misrepresenting him. Bashir denied those accusations.

When Michael's team released additional behind-the-scenes footage, viewers saw a striking contrast between Bashir's private praise and his critical documentary.

The controversy eventually became connected to the criminal proceedings against Jackson. In June 2005, Michael Jackson was acquitted on all counts.

This film explores the interviews, the hidden-camera controversy, the public response, and the complicated relationship between one of the world's biggest entertainers and the journalists who questioned him.
